title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard practices for hiring, employee onboarding, ongoing performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and people managers who onboard and develop ICs and leaders. It includes templates, step-by-step procedures, evaluation rubrics, and escalation points.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time and long-term contractor hires across engineering, product, go-to-market, and central teams.
- Hiring and offer flow covers US, EMEA, and APAC hires (local compliance handled by People Ops).
- Onboarding and performance guidance applies to remote, hybrid, and on-prem employees.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Purpose: Deliver a consistent candidate experience, reduce time-to-offer, and ensure measurable quality of hires. Ownership: hiring manager + people-ops.

Stages (high level):
1. Requisition & role definition
   - Manager opens a requisition in the HRIS and attaches a role spec (see Role Spec template).
   - People Ops verifies headcount and compensation band.
2. Sourcing & screening
   - Recruiter screens and builds candidate slate (minimum 3 qualified candidates recommended).
   - Initial phone screen uses standardized phone-screen template (skills, motivation, logistics).
3. Interview loop
   - Onsite/virtual loop standardized to 3-4 interviews for IC roles, 4-6 for senior/lead roles.
   - Panel includes: hiring manager, peer engineer/product partner, cross-functional stakeholder, and people-ops interviewer for culture & compensation alignment.
   - Use role-specific scorecards (technical/behavioral/impact).
4. Debrief & decision
   - Hiring manager convenes debrief within 48 hours. Decision recorded in ATS with scorecard.
5. Reference checks & offer
   - People Ops performs reference checks for senior roles.
   - Compensation calibrated against band and benchmark data; final approval by People Ops.
6. Offer & negotiation
   - Standard offer letter template used; People Ops owns final sign-off and background check initiation.

Interview standards and scorecards

- All interviewers must complete interviewer training and use the shared scorecard.
- Scorecard fields (flat list): role-fit, technical-skill, problem-solving, communication, collaboration, ownership, overall-recommendation.
- Hiring decision rule: at least 3 raters, no critical failures on safety/compliance questions, and majority 'hire' or 'strong hire'.

Diversity and inclusivity requirements

- Aim for a minimum of two underrepresented candidates in each final slate where feasible.
- Structured interviews and rubrics reduce bias; avoid ranking by impression alone.

2) Offer & compensation guidelines

- Offers must reference the published band and include base, bonus/commission (if applicable), equity summary, and target start date.
- People Ops approves any deviation greater than one band step or >10% above midpoint.
- Standard contingencies: background check, right-to-work verification, and signed confidentiality agreement.

3) Onboarding: 30/60/90 and first week checklist

Objective: Accelerate time-to-productivity and align expectations between manager and new hire. Owner: hiring manager with People Ops support.

First-week checklist (table rendered as plain text):

| Item | Owner | Target timing | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Welcome email & first-day logistics | People Ops | Day -2 | location, equipment, calendar invites |
| Equipment & accounts provisioned | IT/Platform | Day -2 | laptop, monitors, slack, email, VPN, Jira |
| 1:1 with hiring manager | Manager | Day 1 | role expectations, 30/60/90 overview |
| Team intro & product overview | Manager/Team | Day 1 | team goals, codebase tour, repo access |
| Security & compliance training | Security | Day 1-3 | phishing, data handling, access policy |
| New hire orientation session | People Ops | Week 1 | benefits, payroll, policies, culture |

30/60/90 plan (summary):
- 30 days: Learn the product, complete onboarding training, complete 1 small scoped deliverable.
- 60 days: Take ownership of a feature or component, demonstrate competency in primary tools, and contribute to squad rituals.
- 90 days: Independently deliver a project milestone, provide feedback on onboarding, and begin regular goal-oriented 1:1s.

Onboarding activities (recommended list):
- Shadowing sessions with cross-functional partners (support, infra, product).
- Pair programming or documentation deep-dive for engineers.
- Regular manager check-ins (weekly in first 90 days).
- New-hire feedback form at 30 and 90 days (People Ops reviews aggregated feedback quarterly).

4) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence:
- Continuous feedback: ongoing 1:1s (recommended weekly for first 3 months, biweekly thereafter).
- Quarterly check-in: informal progress update between manager and employee.
- Formal performance review: semiannual review cycle (twice per year) with calibration across manager cohort.

Review structure (semiannual):
1. Self-assessment (employee)
2. Manager assessment (using competency rubric)
3. Peer feedback summary (optional depending on role)
4. Calibration meeting (managers + People Ops)
5. Final rating and development plan

Competency rubric (flat list):
- Execution & impact
- Technical depth or role-specific craft
- Collaboration & communication
- Ownership & leadership
- Customer focus (internal and external)

Ratings guidance (recommended language):
- Exceeds expectations: consistently above band-level impact and leads improvements.
- Meets expectations: reliably delivers results and develops skills.
- Below expectations: requires focused development; manager creates Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) if not improved within agreed timeframe.

Performance improvement and escalation

- Low performance timeline: informal coaching (30 days) -> documented performance plan (60-90 days) -> People Ops review -> potential exit if no improvement.
- PIP requirements: clear objectives, measurable success criteria, checkpoints every 2-3 weeks, People Ops sign-off.

Compensation review cycle

- Annual compensation review aligned with fiscal budgeting. Mid-cycle adjustments may be made for promotions, market adjustments, or exceptional retention needs. People Ops and Finance jointly own approvals.

5) Manager responsibilities & best practices

Core expectations:
- Hire and develop talent: run inclusive hiring loops, complete interview training, and provide timely feedback.
- One-on-ones: hold regular 1:1s with agenda and follow-up notes.
- Career conversations: have explicit career and promotion conversations at least quarterly.
- Performance documentation: maintain notes and evidence to support ratings and promotion decisions.
- On-call and time-off coverage: ensure team rotates on-call fairly and approves leave in advance.

Manager toolkit (actions & templates):
- Interview scorecard template (link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples).
- 30/60/90 plan template (copy from People Ops templates kit).
- Promotion packet checklist (role, impact, peer feedback, manager recommendation).
- Offboarding checklist (knowledge transfer plan, account deprovisioning timeline).

6) Promotion and leveling process

- Promotion triggers: sustained impact beyond current band, demonstrated leadership, and cross-functional influence.
- Promotion packet: manager writes a summary + evidence, collects peer feedback, and schedules calibration.
- Calibration: People Ops convenes cross-functional promotion calibration at least quarterly.

7) Templates and artifacts (copy-and-use)

- Role spec template: [internal template link].
- Phone screen script: short questions for alignment & logistics.
- Interview scorecard: standard rubric used across the company.
- Offer letter template: legal-approved wording for US, EMEA, APAC variants.
- 30/60/90 plan template: editable document for managers.
- PIP template: formal performance plan with milestones and dates.

8) Compliance, data & record-keeping

- People Ops retains offer letters, interview scorecards, and background check records per data-retention policy.
- Access to candidate data restricted to hiring panel + People Ops; HRIS enforces role-based access.
- Security training completion required within first week; non-compliance escalated to manager and Security.

9) KPIs & success metrics (People Ops dashboard)

- Time-to-offer: target <= 28 days from req opening to offer.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 70%.
- New hire 90-day retention: target >= 95%.
- Manager training completion: 100% of hiring managers complete interviewer training annually.

10) FAQ & common scenarios

Q: What if a manager needs an urgent hire beyond band?
A: Submit business justification to People Ops; expedited approval may be granted with Finance sign-off.

Q: Who owns relocation & immigration?
A: People Ops coordinates relocation and immigration; manager provides role-specific justification.

Q: How do we handle internal transfers?
A: Internal transfers use an abbreviated hiring loop (shortened interviews, internal reference checks). Compensation adjustments follow promotion/pathway guidelines.

11) Related pages & resources

- People Ops templates library: /confluence/company-handbook/people-ops-templates
- Offer letter & compensation bands: /confluence/finance-and-legal/comp-bands
- Interviewer training course: /learning/interviewer-training

Document ownership and review

- Owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: annual review or after any policy change.
- Change process: submit a doc update request to People Ops via the internal docs backlog.

Appendix: Quick-checklists (copyable)

Manager pre-offer checklist (bullet list):
- Confirm headcount & band with People Ops
- Finalize interview panel and scorecards
- Conduct debrief within 48 hours
- Approve job offer terms with People Ops

New hire 90-day success checklist (bullet list):
- Completed required trainings
- Delivered first scoped project or contribution
- Documented onboarding feedback submitted
- Ongoing development goals set in career conversation

End of document.
